long_biography.plain_text:
Under the name Stefan Michalis Kollakis, Kallakis first came to public notice through a scheme selling bogus manorial titles. After a fraud conviction, he changed his name and recast himself as the head of a supposed property and shipping fortune. He then used special-purpose companies, forged guarantees and inflated lease arrangements to obtain bank loans and acquire prominent commercial buildings.

The structure collapsed when lenders examined the purported guarantees. A jury convicted Kallakis of two conspiracies to defraud in 2013, and the Court of Appeal increased his prison term to eleven years. Later judgments found that he had controlled the property vehicles and rejected attempts to recover interests in the sold portfolio. The Serious Fraud Office has continued pursuing assets traced to the scheme.
